source.title: Deep double descent: where bigger models and more data hurt
source.authors: Preetum Nakkiran; Gal Kaplun; Yamini Bansal; Tristan Yang; B. Barak; I. Sutskever

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation. The text provides figure captions and descriptions, but not the plotted data values themselves.
record.tranche_reason: This is an original empirical study directly sweeping model size, training time, and training-set size and measuring test performance.
record.gate_note: Rows record this study's own experiments. Results cited from prior work are excluded. Where the text gives only a plotted outcome, the value is recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: This is an original source for the claim (arXiv:1912.02292). It directly sweeps model size, training epochs, sample count and weight decay and measures test error. As an original source it gets no verdict labels.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that many of these phenomena often do not occur with optimal early stopping, and that they never observed more data hurting under optimal early stopping. They view label noise as a proxy for model mis-specification rather than as the fundamental cause.
record.recipe_differences: This is the original empirical study. It tests model size, training time, sample count, and other changes as ways of changing effective model complexity.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior and peak location vary with label noise, data augmentation, training-set size, optimizer and learning-rate schedule; the paper also reports that optimal early stopping changes the more-data outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Ensembling 5 models reduces test error most in the critically parameterized regime (Figures 28 and 29).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variance and noise sensitivity of interpolating models is concentrated at the interpolation threshold.

record.problems: Many results are presented as plots without numerical values in the supplied text. The authors state that EMC's tolerance and the width of the critical interval are not yet principled or fully understood.
record.rows_left_out: Additional plotted sweeps and examples are not separately rowed here, including optimizer and learning-rate-schedule variants (Figures 16–18), other early-stopping plots (Figures 19–20, 23–25), adversarial training (Figure 26), and further ensemble comparisons (Figures 28–29). They mostly repeat or extend the recorded qualitative outcomes; the supplied text does not provide separate numerical values for them.

untested.parts: Decision trees, random forests and other non-network model classes. Only random Fourier features are tested beyond deep networks.
Multiple or triple peaks, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Whole version: no re-measurement of complexity by an effective parameter count.
Quantitative prediction of peak location. The tolerance epsilon and the width of the critical interval are heuristic.

missing.what: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with added label noise (5–20%): the noiseless plateau develops into a test-error peak as noise increases.
Model-wise double descent persists under optimal early stopping for ResNet18 on CIFAR-100 with no label noise.
Model-wise double descent in robust test error under adversarial training, with no label noise.
Epoch-wise double descent across Adam, SGD and SGD+Momentum, each with three learning-rate schedules; the peak shifts with the interpolation point.
5-layer CNN on CIFAR-10 with 10% label noise, with and without weight decay 5e-4.

record.verdict_notes: This study is an original source for V1–V3 and V5, so no verdict labels are given. All results are plotted only; the text gives no numbers. Table A in the text is garbled, so per-setting presence or absence (for example r6, r9) cannot be read reliably.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests several listed deep-network families and settings, not all possible architectures, datasets, or training procedures.
The paper tests selected fixed architectures, datasets, and training procedures, not all models or training schedules.
The paper reports cases of more data hurting, plateauing, or helping, but does not establish that more data hurts generally or under optimal early stopping.
The paper tests deep networks and random Fourier features; it does not experimentally sweep every model class.

The paper proposes EMC and reports qualitative alignment of peaks with the interpolation threshold, but does not establish a precise quantitative prediction of peak location across every axis and setting.

It tests how label noise affects the prominence of double descent and reports noiseless examples. It does not test multiple or triple peaks, or whether the peak disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not test whether measuring complexity by an appropriate effective parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
